football_evidence.question: Can Arizona State’s pass rush get to Bear Bachmeier?
football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 0.3 points.
supporting: When Arizona State has the ball (big plays on the ground): Arizona State’s offense turns 8.9% of its runs into explosive gains, and BYU’s defense gives up explosive gains on 5.5% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
In his last two games (Notre Dame and UCF), Bachmeier averaged 7.1 yards per attempt, against 8.9 in his five games before that.
contradicting: When BYU has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): BYU’s offense has allowed a sack on 2.1% of its dropbacks, and Arizona State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 7.6% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
When BYU has the ball (third down): BYU’s offense converts 50.2% of its third downs, and Arizona State’s defense allows opponents to convert 38.1% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).

When BYU has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): BYU’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 13.9% of its runs, and Arizona State’s defense stops 17.2% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).

When Arizona State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Arizona State’s offense has allowed a sack on 7.3% of its dropbacks, and BYU’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.8% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
quarterbacks: Bear Bachmeier has completed 115 of 183 passes (62.8%) for 1,506 yards, 8.2 yards per attempt, 11 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in seven games for BYU, and has been sacked on 4 of 187 dropbacks.

Cutter Boley has completed 104 of 172 passes (60.5%) for 1,360 yards, 7.9 yards per attempt, 13 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in seven games for Arizona State, and has been sacked on 12 of 184 dropbacks.
Mikey Keene has completed 39 of 61 passes (63.9%) for 448 yards, 7.3 yards per attempt, 2 touchdowns and no interceptions in three games for Arizona State, and has been sacked on 5 of 66 dropbacks.
